root_idea.summary: The root preserves three principal lexical branches: drawing out milk or a small yield, delimiting or bounding, and the intestine as a bodily passage.
root_idea.development: The delimitation branch yields مِصْر for a bounded district, city, or country, and derived verbs for establishing or becoming a city. The extraction branch concerns milking or drawing out something gradually, while the anatomical branch is lexicalized in مَصِيرٌ.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The single QAC group contains both the common-noun reading in 2:61 and the proper-name readings referring to Egypt; one normalized headword covers both uses.

senses.definition: A city or town, understood as a bounded settlement in the common-noun use.
senses.usage_conditions: In 2:61, the indefinite form مِصْرًا is read as a city or town; another interpretation takes the word as the proper name Egypt.

senses.definition: Egypt, the country, used as a proper name.
senses.usage_conditions: This proper-name use is represented by the four QAC proper-noun occurrences at 10:87, 12:21, 12:99, and 43:51.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a place a boundary or dividing limit between two things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II; the object may be a town or place made into a مِصْر in the boundary sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To establish, designate, or build a place as a city or town.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II; also used of founding or appointing cities such as al-Basrah and al-Kufah.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give or provide something little by little.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II use describing gradual rather than immediate provision.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a place: to become a city or town.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V in the inchoative or developmental construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A partition, barrier, intervening thing, or boundary between two things or lands.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is مُصُورٌ; the word is also used for boundaries recorded in property contracts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great town or provincial city; in a technical usage, a major settlement where civic, legal, or revenue-distribution functions are carried out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The technical descriptions are lexicographic specifications of a major urban center, not requirements for every use of the word.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The gut or intestine through which food passes from the stomach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The broad sense is intestine; one reported specialization applies the term to certain birds and hoofed animals.
A tropical or figurative lexical usage of the expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To milk by gathering the fingertips over the udder and drawing out the milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action is specifically described as extracting milk from the udder by the fingertips.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To milk the remnants of milk left in the udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can extend to drawing out a scanty yield little by little.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw out or extract a small yield gradually.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used literally of obtaining residual milk and figuratively of drawing on a scanty source of income or benefit.
A lexicalized descriptive use of the passive participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that withholds its milk and does not readily let it out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description concerns milk that is slow to emerge or difficult to extract.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A barrier between two bodies of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived noun belonging to the delimitation branch.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form II establishment or building of cities.
Form V becoming a city or town.
Pointer-only cross-reference with no independent definition in the unit.

cautions: In 2:61, مِصْرًا has a recognized interpretive distinction between the common-noun reading “a city or town” and the proper-name reading “Egypt”; the QAC morphology marks this occurrence as a common noun, while the other four occurrences are proper nouns.
